title: Adaptive CXL.mem-to-LPDDR5X Memory Architecture
summary: Synthesizable Verilog RTL prototype and SystemVerilog UVM verification environment for an adaptive memory path between a CXL.mem-style host interface and an LPDDR5X-oriented controller, aimed at high-performance AI systems.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: An architecture and RTL prototype. It does not claim CXL, PCIe or JEDEC compliance. Any timing values in the design are placeholders and are labelled as non-JEDEC.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.body:
Request path, in order:
- Host / request generator
- CXL.mem transaction interface
- Transaction handler
- Address mapper
- Request buffer
- Adaptive scheduler (age, row locality, read/write mix, priority, refresh)
- LPDDR5X-oriented controller
- Abstract PHY / DRAM interface

sections.heading: Design decisions
sections.body:
- 64 B request line, 512-bit internal data path, byte enables, one tag per request.
- x16 BL16 gives 32 B per burst, so one line takes two bursts. Data width, burst length and channel count are configurable; the first version uses one channel.
- Ordering contract: completion may be out of order across different addresses and is in order for the same address. RTL and scoreboard both enforce it.
- SAME_LINE_STRICT is on by default: a newer request to the same line waits until the older one is done.
- A duplicate outstanding tag is treated as a host protocol violation, flagged by an assertion and a sticky status bit, and must never produce an ambiguous response.
- All design files are plain Verilog (IEEE 1364-2005, .v and .vh). The UVM testbench is SystemVerilog and is kept separate from the RTL.

sections.heading: Verification approach
sections.body: A UVM environment compatible with Questa, plus an RTL-only SystemVerilog smoke test for Verilator. Synopsys VCS is the simulator used for project reviews. The environment is under development; no coverage or pass results are published yet.

sections.heading: Known limitations and open items
sections.body:
- A per-byte write mask is kept in the abstract PHY interface. Compatibility with a real PHY is unresolved; read-modify-write is a documented future change.
- Speculative-read hints are out of scope for the first version.
- An optional occupancy-based output is allowed but is not claimed as a CXL protocol feature.

sections.heading: References
sections.body: CXL-GPU (IEEE Micro, Nov/Dec 2025) and Ramulator 2.0 (IEEE Computer Architecture Letters, 2024).

title: SPI Master–Slave Coverage-Driven Verification
summary: Coverage-driven verification of an SPI master–slave design across all four CPOL/CPHA modes, with a dual-clock error-injection unit and a UVM environment with assertions.

sections.heading: Design
sections.body: Synthesizable RTL for an SPI master–slave pair with an error-injection unit that crosses between two clock domains (synthesizable Verilog-2001). SDC constraints and a synthesis / STA evaluation guide accompany the design.

sections.heading: Verification environment
sections.body: A 16-file UVM environment covering RTL, testbench, SVA assertions and a Makefile, targeting Synopsys VCS and Xcelium. Stimulus covers all four CPOL/CPHA modes.

sections.heading: Tool flow
sections.body: Simulation runs on a university server with Synopsys VCS (R-2020.12-SP2-1) using -full64 -sverilog -debug_access+all. Synthesis uses Fusion Compiler (W-2024.09-SP3).

sections.heading: Debugging notes
sections.body:
- Fixed an LSB bit error caused by changing CPOL/CPHA in the middle of a transaction.
- Fixed a scoreboard pipeline-delay mismatch.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: Coverage and regression results are not published yet. They will be added here once collected from a clean run.

title: TDC-to-SPI Interface with Asynchronous FIFO
summary: FPGA-based interface that moves time-to-digital converter data into an SPI link across clock domains using a dual-clock FIFO with Gray-coded pointers.

sections.heading: Design
sections.body: Dual-clock FIFO with Gray-coded read and write pointers and an almost-full threshold sized for the crossing, written in SystemVerilog RTL.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body: A written report in DOCX and LaTeX is being produced alongside the RTL.

title: 8-bit CDAC Layout in 45 nm CMOS
summary: Analog layout of an 8-bit capacitive DAC in 45 nm CMOS (GPDK 45 nm) using Cadence Virtuoso.

sections.heading: Work so far
sections.body: Bootstrap-switch transistor sizing, derived from a 28 nm pipeline-SAR ADC paper, produced Virtuoso-ready W/L values for the layout.

title: E-TSPC / Heterogeneous CMOS Frequency Divider
summary: E-TSPC / PMOS edge-assist heterogeneous CMOS frequency divider, developed as a project-based-learning assignment for Analog IC Design (MVE321IA).
contribution: Team project with S Rohit, under Dr. Shylashree N.

sections.heading: Deliverables
sections.body: Technical report (with a LaTeX version) and two-phase project presentations.

title: RV32I Processor
summary: A processor that follows the RV32I base integer instruction set, planned as a pipelined RTL design with verification and PPA reporting. Currently in the learning and architecture-study stage.

sections.heading: Status
sections.body: No RTL is published yet. Work so far is studying RISC-V architecture and the five-stage pipeline before implementation.
